questions.q: What is a master (or parent) package?
options: A package whose control flow runs other packages via Execute Package Task
The first package ever created in a project
A package with no Data Flow tasks
A package deployed directly to the SSIS Catalog root folder
questions.explain: A master package's Control Flow is mostly Execute Package Task entries, each one calling a child package to do a specific piece of the overall workflow.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a real benefit of splitting a workflow into master/child packages?
options: It makes the package run using less memory overall
Improved readability and maintenance of each individual piece
Reuse — a child package can be called from several master packages
Independent testing — a child can be run and debugged on its own
questions.explain: Memory usage isn't the reason for this pattern — readability, reuse, security boundaries, and independent testing are the real, documented benefits.

questions.q: How do you make two child packages run in parallel instead of sequentially?
options: Leave their Execute Package Tasks unconnected by any precedence constraint on the Control Flow
Set ExecuteOutOfProcess to True on both
Add both to the same Sequence Container
Parallel execution isn't possible in SSIS — children always run sequentially
questions.explain: Precedence constraints are what force sequential order; two Execute Package Tasks with no constraint connecting them are independent, and SSIS's engine runs them in parallel.

questions.q: Which mechanism lets you pass a value from a parent package to a child package parameter, when both are in the same Project Deployment Model project?
options: Parameter Bindings on the Execute Package Task Editor
The Data Flow Path Editor
SQL Server Agent job step properties
The SSIS Toolbox
questions.explain: The Parameter Bindings page maps a parent variable or parameter directly onto a child package's parameter — this is the modern, Project-Deployment-Model way to pass values down.

questions.q: What's the older mechanism for a child package to read a value from its parent, predating the Project Deployment Model's parameter bindings?
options: The Parent Package Variable configuration type
The SSIS Catalog's environment references
The Data Viewer
The Execute SQL Task's result set
questions.explain: Parent Package Variable is a Package Configuration type (Lesson 39) that lets a child package pull a value straight from a variable defined in its parent — the legacy equivalent of today's parameter bindings.
